page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Lasv4 server family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 15,359 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core and single-core capabilities. The server achieved a top-tier rating in the Geekbench multi-core test and strong performance in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests. Memory performance is mixed; read-only small block cached bandwidth is strong, whereas large block uncached read bandwidth is average. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform reliably, with strong results in Passmark CPU encryption and multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression. For database operations, the server demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests.

Given its massive 15 TB local storage capacity and 512 GB RAM, the L64as_v4 is highly cost-efficient for large-scale database hosting, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. The high resource density of storage and memory relative to the 64 vCPUs reduces the need for external storage attachments, optimizing resource utilization. It is well-suited for relational databases, NoSQL data stores, large-scale software compilation, and medium-sized language model inference tasks.

It features 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores running at 3.7 GHz, and 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. The server is equipped with 15,359 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmarks, the L64as_v4 delivers top-tier Geekbench multi-core performance and strong multi-threaded decompression and database execution. While memory write bandwidth and small-block reads are strong, large-block uncached reads remain average. This hardware profile provides high qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive applications by bundling massive local storage with substantial memory. It is highly suited for large databases, data warehousing, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference workloads.
